items.title: 56679_Arthur Briggs oral history interview
items.q: "what's his name, this wonderful trumpet player that I like so much, 'Red' Nichols. Red Nichols, he started, it was semi-jazz, but I liked him 'cause he had plenty technique and I like that."

ctx.x: Sure. Well, by that time, by 1922, there wasn't much jazz on records, though, was there?

No, no. The "Dixieland" was about the only band that really ventured and made real jazz recordings. Then they -- what's his name, this wonderful trumpet player that I like so much, "Red" Nichols. Red Nichols, he started, it was semi-jazz, but I liked him 'cause he had plenty technique and I like that. And Pollard by the Wolverines, Miff Mole, Bix Beiderbecke, they're the ones that really initiated the world in recordings and everything. They initiated the world.
